title: Ant Group Releases Medical AI Safety Protection Model LingSante MedGuard, Opens Risk Evaluation Dataset

content_html:
On a lab report, lactate dehydrogenase and creatine kinase appear on two adjacent lines. When AI interprets it, it attributes the value of the former to the latter; the indicators, numbers, and units all appear complete, yet the error may propagate through subsequent analysis. Medical scores may be calculated incorrectly, and guidelines that do not apply to the current patient may be cited, all hidden within an answer that looks professional. Risks like these are hard to catch with general-purpose content guardrails alone.

To address hidden risks in medical AI outputs, on November 25, Ant released a medical AI safety protection model, LingSante MedGuard. Combining patient context and a specified review scope, the model identifies potential risks related to medical safety, medical compliance, and medical ethics, provides risk judgments, and pinpoints issues that require review. It is designed for the review stage of medical AI workflows, helping humans with oversight.

To identify these risks, the model must not only read the indicators and values in reports accurately, but also check calculations, guideline applicability conditions, and the permissions of professional roles. During training, the team used one risk-review teacher model and six specialized-capability teacher models to provide judgments and demonstrations respectively, then used two-stage distillation to merge these capabilities into a unified model.

It is reported that Ant also released the LingSante MedGuardBench risk detection dataset, built in collaboration with Shanghai Jiao Tong University. This public version contains 14,588 risk detection records and 578 associated images, divided into three subsets—medical safety, compliance, and ethics—and provides case or medication tasks and reference risk labels for researchers to download and use in follow-up evaluations.

A technical report released by the model team shows that across 11 risk detection tasks in the original experimental system, the LingSante MedGuard 27B version achieved an equally weighted average F1 of 87.4, while the 4B version scored 82.3. These results come from benchmark testing; the model's performance after entering actual service workflows still needs to be continuously tested in specific scenarios.

Beyond model development, the team previously also jointly released the Blue Book on the Ethical Principles System for Anthropomorphic Interactions of Large Models with Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Fudan University. The blue book focuses on ethical risks in anthropomorphic interactions with large models, such as emotional attachment and cognitive erosion, and proposes seven ethical principles and 23 executable rules, offering a reference for interaction boundaries in health AI services.

Recently, Ant has showcased its AI technology layout in the healthcare field, successively open-sourcing multiple healthcare models—including the multimodal model LingSante-3.1-air-VL, the specialized medical reasoning model LingSante-3.1-flash, and the health risk prediction model LingSante Pulse. Among them, the LingSante-3.1-flash model reached open-source SOTA in multiple reasoning, safety alignment, and Agent evaluations. LingSante Pulse is aimed at long-term disease prediction and can predict the risk of 150 diseases over the next six years based on personal sleep data.
